note: Thirty drafts written for the reader's evaluation (specs/product/essays/reviewer.md "Evaluation"): not real students' essays. Each has planted issues labeled by paragraph (0-based, as the notes number them) and the exact words, at least five per category across the set; `accept` names another category a note on that spot may carry and still count; `clean` marks spots that look like errors but are deliberate, where a note is unwarranted. Records and colleges are in colleges-records.json.

drafts.body:
My grandmother could not lift a spoon after her stroke. I watched her try every morning for a month, and every morning she put it down and looked out the window.

I started sketching a brace in the back of my chemistry notebook. Their was no budget and no plan, just a drill, some PVC pipe, and a rubber band that kept snapping.

Through all of this I learned leadership and responsibility and the value of never giving up. I was also on the robotics team, which was fun.

The brace worked for eleven days before the hinge cracked. She used it to eat soup on her birthday, and she laughed when it squeaked.

issues.quote: Their was
issues.label: 'Their' for 'There'

issues.quote: I learned leadership and responsibility and the value of never giving up
issues.label: abstraction with no moment

issues.quote: I was also on the robotics team, which was fun.
issues.label: four years leading robotics mentioned in passing

drafts.body:
I was born on a rainy Tuesday in a small hospital outside Dayton. My parents say I cried louder than any baby on the floor. When I was four, we moved to a house with a red door, and when I was seven I got my first library card.

In ninth grade I joined debate because my friend did. At my first tournament I lost every round.

Losing taught me a myriad of lessons about the plethora of perspectives that exist in our multifaceted world.

No.

What losing taught me was to write down the other side's best argument before my own. I still do it, in debate and at the dinner table.

issues.label: opening starts years before the story

issues.quote: a myriad of lessons about the plethora of perspectives that exist in our multifaceted world
issues.label: thesaurus voice

drafts.body:
My sister Anika was diagnosed with bipolar disorder the winter I turned fourteen. For months our house was quiet in a way I did not understand.

I started running because it was the only hour of the day nobody asked me how I was doing. Cross country became the place I could be tired on purpose.

That year changed my perspective on everything and made me who I am today.

Now, when a patient at the hospital looks scared, I sit down instead of standing over the bed, because I remember what it felt like when the adults in my house stood over me.

prompt.title: Short answer
prompt.text: What is your favorite word, and why? (50 words)

drafts.body: My favorite word is "understudy." In theater the understudy learns every line of a part they will probably never play, and they show up anyway, every night, ready. I was an understudy for two years before I was cast, and those two years taught me more about patience, about listening to other actors, and about loving the work for itself than any role I have played since then.
